subject: Contract exit safety net & fixed-fee penalties request
messages:
From: Alex Novak <alex@acmecloud.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmecloud.com, emma.rivera@acmecloud.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA - request for termination & fixed-fee penalties

Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we scope our procurement and present to our procurement committee next week, a couple of legal asks came up that I wanted to surface early so we can avoid rework during contracting.

High level asks from Acme Cloud:
- If Redwood misses the target uptime (we are asking for 99.95% per month), we need the option to terminate for convenience with a pro-rated refund and a fixed fee penalty for repeated severity-1 outages (they want a fixed $50k per repeat major outage beyond remediation credits).
- Alternatively, if Redwood will not accept termination rights, we need an escrowed fee-at-risk equal to 3 months' committed fees that we can draw on for severe or repeated failures.

We understand these are material asks, but given the regulatory nature of our service, the committee wants contractual levers beyond service credits. Can you flag who on your side should be involved (legal / sales / leadership)? We can provide a short redline showing where they want these inserted.

Appreciate quick thoughts — procurement deadline is 11 May.

Best,
Alex
Director, Platform Ops
Acme Cloud

Attachments: acme_sla_redlines.pdf
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Redwood SLA - request for termination & fixed-fee penalties

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's note. They want termination rights or an escrowed fee-at-risk (3 months) plus a fixed $50k per repeat S1 outage. Procurement deadline 11 May.

Initial thoughts: we typically offer credits and a tiered SLO remedy up to material breach cures, but termination for convenience tied to SLO misses is tough. Fixed per-outage cash penalties are also outside our standard playbook.

Can we identify acceptable counteroptions (e.g., enhanced credits + limited buyout cap, defined cure windows, and a one-time right to exit after X months with notice)? Also need legal appetite on escrow mechanics and how to limit exposure.

I can join a call with their procurement team next week if helpful.

- Nikhil
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood SLA - request for termination & fixed-fee penalties

Nikhil — thanks for flagging. My take:
- Termination for repeated SLO failures: we can consider a narrowly scoped right to terminate for material breach if we fail to meet a sustained, measurable degradation (e.g., >= 3 severity-1 incidents in 60 days with missed remediation windows), but not termination for a single missed monthly availability tier.
- Fixed $50k per repeat outage: not acceptable as-is. Instead propose an escalating credit + capped cash makewhole (e.g., credit equivalent plus a buyout cap equal to 2 months' committed fees) to give them commercial comfort while limiting our downside.
- Escrowed fee-at-risk: we could entertain escrow mechanics but only as a security deposit, not freely payable; release conditions must be narrow and tied to adjudicated breach events.

I suggest we prepare a one-page counter: 1) propose termination after defined threshold events, 2) remove flat per-outage cash penalties and replace with capped buyout or enhanced credits, 3) escrow only as a conditional security instrument. Karthik, please advise on specific legal language and whether Finance would accept a 2-month cap.

Marissa
VP, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, alex@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract exit safety net & fixed-fee penalties request

Alex — thanks for the transparency and helpful redlines. Looping in legal counsel (cc'd) on high-level response. Quick positions from Redwood legal:

1) Termination: Redwood is willing to accept a limited termination right tied to a defined, sustained failure pattern (suggested threshold: three Severity 1 incidents within any rolling 90-day window where remediation fails to meet contractual cure timelines). This is termination for cause (not convenience) and follows a 30-day cure period after the triggering event chain is identified. We will not accept immediate termination for a single monthly availability miss.

2) Cash penalties: we cannot agree to open-ended per-outage liquidated damages. We can offer a fallback commercial remedy: enhanced service credits plus a buyout option capped at the lesser of 3 months' committed fees or $150k, whichever is lower, payable only after the defined triggering pattern and failure to cure.

3) Escrow: acceptable as an alternative security mechanism provided funds are held in a mutually agreed escrow agent with clear release criteria aligned to adjudicated breach events. Escrow amount should mirror the buyout cap.

4) Audit & evidence: any claims to draw escrow or trigger buyout must be supported by objective telemetry, shared post-incident RCA, and a joint review process.

Please confirm if Acme is willing to accept the threshold language and capped buyout in lieu of per-outage fixed penalties. If yes, we can produce redline language and a proposed escrow exhibit for review.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Novak <alex@acmecloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, nikhil_sharma@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract exit safety net & fixed-fee penalties request

Karthik / team — appreciate the quick positions. Two points from our side after internal review:
- The procurement committee will not accept a carve that requires adjudication or prolonged cure periods without a pragmatic exit path. They prefer a deterministic mechanism (either termination after X events OR an escrow draw mechanism that is straightforward to execute).
- On the buyout cap: Acme prefers 3 months' committed fees as the maximum, and would like the $150k floor removed (they want the math to be strictly based on committed spend).

Next step: Can you send a short redline we can circulate to procurement/finance by Wednesday (5 May)? If Redwood can agree to termination after 3 S1 incidents in 60 days OR escrow draw equal to 3 months' committed fees with clearly defined release conditions, we should be able to move forward.

Thanks — Alex
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
To: Alex Novak <alex@acmecloud.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract exit safety net & fixed-fee penalties request

Alex — thanks for the clarity. We can do the following as a near-final commercial position to get procurement comfortable:

1) Termination for cause tied to sustained failure: three Severity 1 incidents in any rolling 60-day window where Redwood fails to meet the agreed remediation commitments and post-incident RCA demonstrates systemic platform failure. Termination follows a 30-day opportunity to cure after the third incident.

2) Alternative security: escrow equal to 3 months' committed fees (no $150k floor). Funds held with mutual escrow agent; release only on a defined panel decision after joint review and meeting objective telemetry thresholds.

3) No per-outage flat cash penalty. Instead, a capped buyout (the escrow) or termination as above.

4) We will provide a redline and an escrow exhibit by EOD Thursday (6 May). Please confirm procurement is ok with the 30-day cure window after the threshold triggers — that is a non-negotiable operational protection for us.

If procurement needs a deterministic immediate draw instead of an adjudicated release, we'll need to escalate to Finance/Legal leadership to approve an alternate escrow flow.

Regards,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_escrow_terms.xlsx; DocuSign: https://docusign.com/s/Acme-Redwood-SLA-Exhibit
